warnings: This house's structural footprint is a single 8.00m x 8.00m square (grid 1-3 x A-C, 3x3 column grid, 9 footings). Two DIFFERENT sets of offset/eave lines exist around it at two different elevations, both real but easy to conflate: (1) at ROOF/ring-beam level, S-04 and S-05 print a symmetric 1.50m offset on all 4 sides carrying the real ring beam RB1 (steel-roofed hip structure on an RC ring beam) — these became dummy grids 1'/3'/A'/C'. (2) at FLOOR-PLAN level, S-03 prints a north offset of only 1.10m and east/west offsets of 1.50m, all with NO beam landing on them (just the printed roofline/eave projection 'แนวหลังคา') — recorded in unassigned_dimensions/non_grid_dimensions_do_not_confuse, not as dummy grids, per the 'do not invent a dummy for a slab-only/roofline edge' rule. The x-axis 1.50m floor-level roofline offset happens to numerically match the real roof-level RB1 offset at the same position — a genuine coincidence, flagged in non_grid_dimensions_do_not_confuse so it isn't mistaken for the same structural line.

South of grid C, the floor plan (S-03) ALSO prints a real beam (B5, and beam ends of B6X/BX) at C+1.50m — this is the same 1.50m offset as the roof ring beam's south run, so dummy grid 'C-prime' (C') serves double duty: it is both S-04's roof-level RB1 south run AND S-03's floor-level ramp/entry-deck beam B5. Both source sheets are listed on this line's usage. Beyond C' by a further 3.50m (to A-to-south-edge = 13.00m total) is an unroofed, unframed slab-on-grade deck (element_type slab, marker 'S0') with no beam at its outer edge — per the beam-endpoint rule, no dummy grid was added there.

Total-row cross-check (§4): S-03's own outer y-axis dimension bracket reads '13.00' — this LOOKS like it might be a mis-print at first glance (the naive read 'edge-to-C' would be 1.10+4.00+4.00=9.10, not 13.00), but re-tracing the bracket's actual tick marks shows it starts at grid A (not the -1.10 roofline edge) and runs to the south slab edge: 4.00(A-B)+4.00(B-C)+1.50(C-C')+3.50(C'-southedge) = 13.00 exactly. Separately, the architecture floor plan (A-04, out of op04 scope but checked for this cross-check per op01's precedence rules) prints '14.10' for the FULL north-roofline-edge-to-south-slab-edge span: 1.10+13.00=14.10, also exact. Both printed totals are correct; they simply measure from two different start points. No actual transcription error — flagged here only because the two numbers looked contradictory before re-verifying the bracket endpoints against a 2x zoom crop.

Two interior secondary beams — B1 (splits several rooms into a north/south pair, e.g. inside the 1-2 x B-C bathroom cluster and again inside the 2-3 x A-B bedroom-2/laundry cluster) and B2 (splits the 1-2 x B-C room into east/west halves) — have NO printed dimension anywhere in the structural set (S-02 through S-10) locating their exact offset from the main grid; only their existence, mark, and rebar spec (S-09) are given. The architecture floor plan (A-04, viewed only for context, not extracted) shows a small ห้องน้ำ/bathroom partition roughly in that area but likewise carries no explicit dimension to B1/B2's position. Per '§4 pos_m is always read from an actually-printed dimension line — never guessed', no dummy grid was invented for B1 or B2; their occurrences on the plan_beam file are recorded with span_source:'unresolved' and an approximate/descriptive grid_ref instead, matching the precedent set by house #07's B2 interior beam.

No soil_boring_log sheet and no dedicated plan_column sheet in this set — columns appear only as marks on the footing plan (S-02) and in the column schedule (S-07), matching op04's own note that this is the expected/common case.

dummy_grid_rule_check.before_origin_naming: 1' (x=-1.50, west of grid 1) and A' (y=-1.50, north of grid A) both fall before the first main grid line on their axis. Per §4's negative-pos_m exception they are still named after the nearest main grid (1 and A respectively, not left/above-blank), matching the spec's own worked example.
dummy_grid_rule_check.after_last_naming: 3' (x=9.50, east of grid 3) and C' (y=9.50, south of grid C) are named after the main grid to their left/above (3 and C respectively), per the standard rule.
